title: Determinants of Household Energy Choices in Somalia: Applied Multinomial Logistic Regression Model
venue_or_publisher: International Journal of Energy Economics and Policy 16(1), 499–506
geographic_scope: Somalia; urban, rural and nomadic households in SIHBS coverage
method: Multinomial logit; 7,212 households; main lighting and cooking fuels
key_findings: Table 3 reports charcoal 47.9%, firewood 41.3% and gas 5.7%; residence and socioeconomic characteristics are associated with fuel choice.
limitations: Main-fuel responses miss fuel stacking and quantities; cross-sectional associations are not adoption effects. Narrative and Table 4 contain discrepancies.
project_relevance: Starting specification for survey reanalysis; preserve three residence categories.
verification_locator: PDF pp.3–6 / journal pp.501–504, sections 3–4, Tables 3–5; Table 3 visually checked. Issue year 2026; landing page publication 2025-12-26.
quality_appraisal: Useful survey-based evidence; rerun weighting and coefficients before calibration.
data_code_availability: Underlying SIHBS through SNBS; no analysis code verified.

title: Household Solid Fuel Use and Associated Factors in Somaliland: A Multilevel Analysis of Data From 2020 Somaliland Demographic and Health Survey
geographic_scope: Somaliland survey; five regions in analysis table; urban, rural, nomadic
data_period: 2020 survey edition; fieldwork dates not independently verified
key_findings: Reports 97.2% in its polluting/solid-fuel category and 2.8% clean; education, wealth and cooking location associated with choices.
limitations: Classifies kerosene as 'solid'. Its prevalence differs from original-survey figures it cites; exclusions, coding and weighting need reconciliation.
verification_locator: Methods: Study participants, Outcome variable; Table 1; Background paragraphs citing SLDHS; Tables 2–5.
quality_appraisal: Relevant large survey reanalysis; not a national Somalia benchmark or physical solid-fuel share.
data_code_availability: Underlying survey referenced; public analysis code not verified.

title: Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice Regarding Charcoal Consumption among Households in Sanaag Province, North-Eastern Somalia
geographic_scope: Badhan town, five wards, Sanaag; not province-wide probability coverage
data_period: Summer survey; calendar year not established from inspected methods
method: Face-to-face KAP questionnaire; purposive town selection, systematic household sampling; n=343
data_sources: Primary household interviews; questionnaire pretest and pilot
key_findings: Charcoal and firewood dominated; LPG 21.3% as primary fuel. Knowledge correlated with reported practice, but attitude did not.
limitations: Self-reported practice; purposive location; low pilot practice reliability and demographic-table inconsistencies. Not a tested behavioral intervention.
project_relevance: Design locally appropriate surveys of fuel stacking and affordability.
verification_locator: Sections 2.1–2.5, 3.2 and 3.6; PDF pp.3–5,11; p.5 visually checked.
quality_appraisal: Valuable local primary evidence with limited geographic transfer.
data_code_availability: No respondent-level dataset or analysis code verified.

title: Smoke exposure risk among Somali households: prevalence, determinants, and regional disparities
geographic_scope: Somalia SHDS sampled areas; urban, rural and nomadic
data_sources: SHDS household fuel and cooking-location responses
key_findings: Classifies 60.34% high and 36.32% medium smoke-exposure risk; higher wealth and urban residence can coincide with higher risk.
limitations: Risk is constructed from fuel/location, not measured PM2.5, personal exposure or clinical outcomes; cross-sectional and coding-dependent.
project_relevance: Add ventilation and cooking location to energy surveys.
verification_locator: Methods: Study variables, Data analysis; Results: Prevalence; Figures 1–2; Discussion/limitations.
quality_appraisal: Useful risk-screening framework; cannot establish disease effects or sensor-measured pollution.
data_code_availability: Survey access referenced; no reproducible analysis code verified.

title: Analysing rural and urban differences in modern cooking energy use in Somalia using the Fairlie decomposition method
geographic_scope: SIHBS 17 regions excluding Middle Jubba; nomadic merged into rural
method: Logistic regression and Fairlie decomposition; n=7,212
key_findings: Reports 10.4% 'modern' cooking and a 12.553 percentage-point rural–urban gap under its definitions.
limitations: Paraffin is 'modern'; not SDG clean cooking. Section 3.3/Table 3 gives urban OR 5.211 with CI 1.410–1.891; intervals and estimates are incompatible on a common scale.
project_relevance: Important prior inequality analysis; quarantine effect-size benchmarks pending correction.
quality_appraisal: Definitions and numerical reporting prevent direct calibration; descriptive reanalysis remains useful.

title: Spatial and multilevel analysis of household solid fuel use and its determinants in Somalia using the 2020 demographic and health survey
geographic_scope: Somalia SHDS coverage; Table 1 lists 16 regions
method: Multilevel logit; Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi*; Table 1 totals 13,321 households
key_findings: Reports 95.05% solid-fuel use and regional clustering; education, services and wealth associated with choices.
limitations: Abstract labels poor-versus-rich OR 0.11 in a misleading direction; full-text p.7 correctly associates it with rich versus poor. Missingness, weights and geographic coverage need replication.
project_relevance: Existing spatial cooking-fuel study; avoid claiming novelty for another hotspot map alone.
verification_locator: PDF pp.3–8,13; outcome definition section 2.4; Table 1; p.7 visually checked against abstract.
quality_appraisal: Useful method, but prefer full-text model definitions over abstract prose.
data_code_availability: SNBS survey access referenced; code not verified.

title: Environmental sustainability in Somalia: the role of clean cooking energy and remittances on ecological footprints
method: SADF tests, time-varying Granger analysis, kernel regularized least squares
data_sources: Global Footprint Network; CEIC cooking access; Federal Reserve remittances; WDI; SESRIC; KOF
key_findings: Finds negative statistical associations between clean-cooking access/remittances and ecological footprint.
limitations: Short macro series, secondary/model-derived indicators and omitted conflict/institutional variables limit causal inference. Granger causality is predictive ordering, not intervention identification.
project_relevance: Prior macroeconomic literature; supports hypotheses, not household adoption coefficients.
verification_locator: Data and methods; Discussion; Conclusion/limitations; Data availability.
quality_appraisal: Interpret cautiously; microdata and policy evaluation needed for causal claims.
data_code_availability: Data available on request; no downloadable code verified.

title: Assessment of charcoal driven deforestation rates in a fragile rangeland environment in North Eastern Somalia using very high resolution imagery
method: Very-high-resolution imagery, fieldwork, visual sampling and semi-automatic tree detection
data_sources: Satellite images and field observations described in author-institution abstract
key_findings: Reports approximately 2.8% annual tree loss and no regrowth during the sampled interval.
limitations: Local historical study, not national annual deforestation; full methods unavailable for this review.
project_relevance: Foundational method and historical benchmark for local charcoal-ecology monitoring.
verification_locator: FAO SWALIM author-institution abstract: https://faoswalim.org/content/assessment-charcoal-driven-deforestation-rates-fragile-rangeland-environment-north-eastern ; publisher full text blocked.
quality_appraisal: Important historical evidence; appraisal limited to institutional abstract and bibliographic checks.

title: Mapping charcoal driven forest degradation during the main period of Al Shabaab control in Southern Somalia
geographic_scope: Two Lower Juba sample areas, 32 and 39 km²
method: Visual kiln-site counts and conversion assumptions to infer tree loss
data_sources: Very-high-resolution satellite imagery; kiln/tree conversion parameters
key_findings: Finds expanding kiln activity and estimated tree loss above 7% over five years in sampled areas.
limitations: Kilns proxy tree removal; small selected areas and assumed conversion parameters prevent national extrapolation.
project_relevance: Trace charcoal supply-chain ecology and uncertainty in kiln-to-wood conversion.
verification_locator: FAO-hosted accepted PDF pp.1–5, Table 1; JRC DOI and authors verified. JRC deposit 2014 differs from journal year 2013.
quality_appraisal: Transparent historical proxy approach; no causal attribution from kiln imagery alone.
data_code_availability: Source imagery and underlying GIS not downloaded.

title: Rapid mapping and impact estimation of illegal charcoal production in southern Somalia based on WorldView-1 imagery
geographic_scope: 4,700 km² along the Juba River, southern Somalia
method: Object-based kiln detection; visual-reference validation in 419 sampled 1 km² clusters; parameter ranges
data_sources: 0.5 m WorldView-1 images; literature and local knowledge
key_findings: Estimates 24,000 tonnes charcoal and 2.7% tree loss over two years for the study area.
limitations: Security prevented field validation. Kiln geometry, wood density, moisture and conversion efficiency drive inferred tonnage.
project_relevance: Strong candidate method for remotely monitoring supply; independently calibrate conversion factors.
verification_locator: University-hosted publisher PDF pp.3–7; validation and wood-volume methods; Tables 2–3.
quality_appraisal: Explicit validation and assumptions improve traceability; inferred production remains model-dependent.
data_code_availability: Publisher PDF available through University of Twente; raw imagery not acquired.

title: Automatic detection of charcoal kilns on Very High Resolution images with a computer vision approach in Somalia
venue_or_publisher: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation 125, 103524
method: Faster R-CNN trained on curated expert-labeled kiln images
data_sources: FAO expert delineations; panchromatic and RGB very-high-resolution imagery
key_findings: JRC abstract reports precision 90% for panchromatic and 80% for RGB imagery.
limitations: Precision is not overall accuracy, recall or unbiased total production. Full text/data splits not inspected.
project_relevance: Existing machine-vision method; novelty should concern transfer, uncertainty or new monitoring application.
verification_locator: JRC author-institution abstract and metadata; DOI verified; publisher full-text request failed.
quality_appraisal: Promising scalable detection, with evaluation limited to repository abstract.
data_code_availability: JRC page displayed no downloadable dataset/code.

title: Remote Sensing Based Quantification of Forest Cover Change in Somalia for the Period 2000 to 2019
method: Google Earth Engine analysis of Landsat-based forest-cover products; 30% canopy threshold
key_findings: Maps forest-cover change and supplies an Earth Engine script link.
limitations: Abstract 2000 forest area 87,294 ha conflicts with section 3.1's 8,729,400 ha: factor 100. Forest loss is not uniquely charcoal-caused.
project_relevance: Reproduce and audit definitions/area units before using forest-stock estimates.
verification_locator: Abstract; sections 2.2–3.2; section 3.1 script link. Publisher date 15 October 2021 retained; Crossref reports 2022 (bibliographic discrepancy independently verified by coordinating review).
quality_appraisal: Numerical national-area benchmark quarantined pending unit reconciliation.

title: Biodigester Market Assessment in Somalia
geographic_scope: Somalia; includes Mogadishu, livestock ports, Somaliland and Puntland
data_period: Mixed 2020–2022 contextual data and site consultations; publication date unresolved; catalogue posted February 2025
method: Market reconnaissance, stakeholder/company profiles and feedstock-based potential calculations
data_sources: Interviews, site visits, livestock statistics and company information
key_findings: Confirms six identified digesters: four active, two inactive; separately estimates 62,000 potential units.
limitations: Small identified inventory is not a census. Feedstock access, water, competing uses and financing constrain modeled potential.
project_relevance: Useful supplier/site leads; inspect operating units before adopting performance or potential.
verification_locator: PDF pp.2,6–8,14–27; p.7 visually checked; ABC programme links original report.
quality_appraisal: Useful reconnaissance; technical potential must remain distinct from practical uptake.
data_code_availability: Company profiles in report; no raw survey dataset/code verified.

title: Terminal Evaluation: Federal Government of Somalia and United Nations Joint Programme for Sustainable Charcoal Reduction and Alternative Livelihoods (PROSCAL) — Final Evaluation Report
geographic_scope: Somalia; consultations concentrated in Hargeisa and Mogadishu
method: Document review, field visits, nonrandom stakeholder interviews and online questionnaires
data_sources: Programme reports, beneficiaries, companies and institutions
key_findings: LPG companies reported purchases declined after subsidy withdrawal; evaluation rates sustainability moderately likely.
limitations: Small uneven nonrandom consultations and implementer statistics; no counterfactual or measured exposure trial.
project_relevance: Prioritize refill affordability and sustained use over distribution counts.
verification_locator: Sections 1.3–1.4, 3.3.7, 3.3.10; printed pp.3–5,50–52 (PDF pp.17–19,64–66); p.52 visually checked.
quality_appraisal: Strong for implementation mechanisms, weaker for causal impact or prevalence.

title: UN Somalia Joint Fund Final Progress Report: Sustainable Charcoal Reduction and Alternative Livelihoods (PROSCAL)
geographic_scope: Somalia; Benadir, federal member states and Somaliland
data_period: 1 April 2016–31 March 2023; publication date not established, hosted in 2024 directory
data_sources: Implementer monitoring, activities and terminal evaluation
key_findings: Reports support for 34,863 efficient-stove households and 14,211 subsidized-LPG households; also solar water heating and alternative livelihoods.
limitations: Beneficiary totals are reported outputs, not verified exclusive fuel switching, emission savings or durable adoption; overlaps need checking.
project_relevance: Locate implementers and follow-up samples; compare with terminal evaluation.
verification_locator: Cover; executive summary; PDF pp.6–9 and results narrative.
quality_appraisal: Useful original programme record; not independent impact evaluation.
data_code_availability: Report public; underlying beneficiary/monitoring data not verified.

title: Cooking with Power, The Somali eCookbook: Traditional Somali Recipes Tested with Modern Electric Cooking
venue_or_publisher: Modern Energy Cooking Services (MECS), Loughborough University
geographic_scope: Somali recipes; full-text test geography unverified. Programme announcement identifies Sheder camp, Ethiopia; do not adopt as Somalia field data.
data_period: Published 6 August 2026; test dates not verified
method: Publisher describes recipe tests using modern electric cooking; detailed protocol inaccessible
data_sources: MECS publisher landing page and first-party programme discovery announcement
key_findings: A dedicated Somali eCooking recipe-test publication exists; numerical energy and cost results were not inspected.
limitations: Download inaccessible; no verified sample size, tariff, appliance settings or performance values.
project_relevance: High-priority acquisition for culturally relevant controlled cooking tests; requires local transfer checks.
verification_locator: MECS official publication page, title, author and date; linked download failed; first-party announcement discovery only.
quality_appraisal: Verified publication identity; insufficient access for quantitative appraisal.
data_code_availability: Download linked but not obtained; no data/code verified.

title: Cooking Fuel and the Humanitarian Response in the Horn of Africa: Key Messages and Guidance for Action
geographic_scope: Regional humanitarian response including Somalia; concrete assessment examples are Dadaab/Kakuma, Kenya
method: Operational guidance drawing on SAFE assessment and humanitarian practice
data_sources: Women's Refugee Commission / WFP SAFE experience
key_findings: Argues food assistance must include cooking-fuel access, protection, livelihood and environmental considerations.
limitations: Guidance, not Somalia intervention evaluation; historical regional context and Kenyan examples must remain labeled.
project_relevance: Integrate fuel expenditure, collection safety and food preparation into displacement research.
verification_locator: Both PDF pages; Emergency response, Food and Nutrition, Protection and Longer-term response.
quality_appraisal: Useful conceptual framework; no direct transfer of fuel-saving percentages.
data_code_availability: Two-page brief public; no Somali microdata.

title: A Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Household Smoke Exposure Risk in Somalia: An Analysis With SHAP Explanations
method: Six classifiers; 80/20 split, cross-validation and SHAP; weighted n=15,838
data_sources: SHDS fuel/location-derived binary risk, household covariates
key_findings: Gradient boosting reports AUC 0.81; weighted binary risk prevalence 70%.
limitations: Reuses SHDS, not independent exposure measurements; binary risk differs from earlier ordinal categories. Random holdout does not establish spatial/temporal transfer.
project_relevance: Existing ML risk study; prioritize measured validation rather than novelty by algorithm substitution.
verification_locator: Methods: outcome, preprocessing, training/evaluation; Table 2; Discussion and data availability.
quality_appraisal: Useful predictive comparison; no evidence of external pollution/health validation in inspected sections.
data_code_availability: Survey source referenced; no directly downloadable analysis code verified.

title: Evaluation of the Methane (CH4) Generation Rate Constant (k Value) of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) in Mogadishu City, Somalia
geographic_scope: Mogadishu; 204 households across 17 districts grouped into three zones
data_period: September 2022–March 2023 stated; seven continuous collection days also stated, leaving seasonal timing unclear
method: Household waste weighing/sorting, density and oven-dried moisture; composition-based first-order methane-decay coefficients
data_sources: Primary household waste samples; external decay coefficients described as IPCC-based
key_findings: Reports mean waste generation of 0.2 kg/person/day and food waste as the largest component; methane kinetics are calculated.
limitations: Ambiguous sampling timeline; coefficient choices need reconciliation with Table 3; no measured gas capture, energy yield or operating biogas plant.
project_relevance: Local feedstock-characterization lead; requires seasonal verification and conversion/recovery testing before energy-potential use.
verification_locator: Publisher PDF pp.1,6–11,17–18; sections 2.1–2.4, 3.1 and 4; Tables 2–3; equation 9. Pages 6 and 10 visually checked. Published 6 October 2023.
quality_appraisal: Measured feedstock evidence is useful; numerical gas estimates require a separate parameter audit.
data_code_availability: Authors state all data are in the manuscript; no machine-readable household file or analysis code verified.
